full_judgment:
Md. Ismailuddin Sarker J: This petition for leave by the pre-emptor-petitioners is from the judgment and order dated August 3, 1984 passed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1260 of 1993 affirming the judgment and order passed by the Additional District Judge, Jhenidah, by his Judgment and order dated January 31, 1993 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 33 of 1986 affirming those passed by the Assistant Judge, Shailakupa rejecting an application for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 5. Mr. Fazlul Karim, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners, has contended that the learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in holding that cousin sister's son is a relation by consanguinity within three degrees from the donor and the transaction in question is covered by sub-section 10(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The learned Counsel submitted that the degree of consanguinity is to be computed under section 28 of the Succession Act, 1925 read with schedule 1 thereof. In support of his contention Mr. Karim has referred to a Single Bench decision of the Dhaka High Court in the case of Tamizunnessa vs. Umar Ali reported in 18 DLR 572 wherein it has been held that the mode of reckoning of the degrees of consanguinity is to be done under section 28 of the Succession Act, 1925 read with the first schedule thereof. But the learned Judge did not notice that section 23 of the Succession Act provides that nothing in this part i e, "of consanguinity" shall apply to any Hindu, Muhammadan, Buddhist, Sikh and Jain or Parsi. This has been noticed by another Single Judge of the Dhaka High Court in the case of Sale Mohammed vs. Mosammat Ayesha Khatoon Choudhurani 20 DLR 376. In the case reported in 18 DLR 572 both the learned Advocates for the parties agreed that degrees of consanguinity have to be computed in the mode prescribed by section 28 read with the first schedule without noticing the provision of section 23 of the said Act. But this decision was not followed in the latter decision reported in 20 DLR 376, wherein it has been held that sister's son is a relation by consanguinity within three degrees of his donor. In the instant case the parties are Muslims and the principle of Succession Act 1925 is not applicable. The concept of consanguinity in Muhammadan Law is different from that which is prevailing amongst the Christians. The learned Judge of the High Court Division applied the principle enunciated in the case reported in 20 DLR 376 and rightly held that a cousin sister's son is within three degrees of consanguinity from the donor. Hence the contention of Mr. Fazlul Karim cannot be accepted.
